messages.subject: trouble with optimizing with DEC+J model
messages.subject_clean: trouble with optimizing with DEC+J model
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Matzke,

Can you please let me know if there is anything wrong in my code?   I made R program ( I just copied some codes from your tutorials) to analyze Anolis data that were uploaded  in https://datadryad.org/stash/dataset/doi:10.5061%2Fdryad.2mc1t

In my program (22nd line of anolis_test_dec.r),  "jumpOption" represents DEC model (=F) or DEC+J model (=T).  After running with two models, I compared the obtained results with those uploaded in Dryad (attached 'MVD_2013_Anolis_DEC_vs_DECj_M0_v1.pdf').

With DEC model, the log-likelihood score that I got is -275.88, which is same as that of Dryad.  However, with DEC+J model, I got log-likelihood of -810.34. This is much lower than that of DEC model and much different from that of Dryad.  Maybe some trouble occurs during optimization with DEC+J.   I'm attaching two figure files that I got with DEC, DEC+J (Anolis_DEC.pdf and Anolis_DECj.pdf).  I used my R program for some other data sets, and those looked OK, but I get trouble with Anolis data.

Could you please give me advice about how to avoid this kind of optimization trouble?

Sincerely,
Tae-Kun Seo

messages.body_plain:
Hi Tae-Kun,

I just ran it with the default script at: http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

...assuming 3 areas max. I got:

DEC lnL = -275.8841
DEC+J lnL = -241.9379

...which seems reasonable.  The script from the 2013 paper is probably very old at this point, and might have used an old optimizer or settings (I don't remember, but the various optimizer packages have had many updates since then, they are designed by other people, not me).

I'm attaching my script & results -- cheers!
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Dear Nick,

Thank you for your prompt reply.

In the default script,  Biogeobears uses parameter estimates with DEC as initial values for DEC+J model optimization.  In my case, I'm trying to optimize with DEC+J model without running with DEC (I am doing this within my simulation work).  In many cases, running DEC+J without DEC's estimates was fine. But, for the case of Anolis, optimization doesn't properly work.  I guess this may be the problem of Gensa library.

Sincerely,
Tae-Kun

messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] trouble with optimizing with DEC+J model
messages.body_plain:
Hi -- yes, sometimes on rare occasions I've found that GenSA does weird things, but then, I've found that for all optimizers. use_optimx = TRUE may work if $use_optimx = "GenSA" gives weird results.

In general, one always should be thinking about the optimization results and if they make sense (ie. DEC+J lnL always has to be equal or higher than DEC lnL).  It looks like you are doing this!

Cheers,
Nick

messages.subject: Re: Error: object 'tipranges' not found"
messages.body_plain:
I have also had this error.  It seems to be related to some unfortunate combination of R version, package version, and OS version. I haven't updated R in a while to avoid breaking things, so have R 4.0.2. I also haven't updated BioGeoBEARS recently. I have, however, updated Windows to 11 relatively recently; I'm not sure if that's why.   I could only solve it by using a clean updated install of R (on a different machine with Windows 10, so I can't say if the R version was the actual problem). Have you tried updating R, Alessandro?

Here are my debugging notes so far, and would love if anyone can suggest a simple alternative to updating R, or give any other insights.

The error:

> tipranges = getranges_from_LagrangePHYLIP(lgdata_fn=geogfn)

Error in validObject(.Object) :   invalid class “tipranges” object: superclass "Mnumeric" not defined in the environment of the object's class

I tracked this to the call to new(), the R function for instantiating an object of a specific class, in define_tipranges_object() within the above call. There’s nothing wrong with the input, it happens before that input is even added to the generic object.

Here's the class:

> getClass("tipranges")

Class "tipranges" [package "BioGeoBEARS"]

 Slots:

  Name:       .Data         df

Class:    numeric data.frame

 Extends:

Class "numeric", from data part

Class "vector", by class "numeric", distance 2

Class "index", by class "numeric", distance 2

Class "replValue", by class "numeric", distance 2

Class "numLike", by class "numeric", distance 2

Class "number", by class "numeric", distance 2

Class "atomicVector", by class "numeric", distance 2

Class "numericVector", by class "numeric", distance 2

Class "numeric or NULL", by class "numeric", distance 2

Class "replValueSp", by class "numeric", distance 3

Class "Mnumeric", by class "numeric", distance 3

This is the only earlier result for that exact BGB error that I could find: https://groups.google.com/g/biogeobears/c/DgYTl14NAAY/m/aZrqOFbbCAAJ

And the only suggestions seem to be to update and reinstall everything.

I also found this error mentioned for a different R class and OS (mac) on a different forum: https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/4436 which suggests installing an older version of the package “Matrix”. However this post was in 2021 and I’ve used the BGB code successfully since then (though I don't know if my Matrix was updated by another package recently). I have Matrix 1.4-1. I haven't tried to do anything with it yet.

Also suggested here: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69283444/error-in-validobject-object-invalid-class-dsparsemodelmatrix-object-super

Thanks,

Anne
